**The Mac app works.** Drives now unlock on current macFUSE (5.3 and later),
Finder can copy files onto them, and browsing folders is faster. Tested on a
real Mac: macOS 27.2, macFUSE 5.5.0, Apple Silicon.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.3.2-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.3.2-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Fixed

- **Unlocking on macFUSE 5.3 and later** failed with "Unspecified Error".
  The mount call cloak used stopped working in macFUSE 5.3; cloak now mounts
  through macFUSE's regular call.
- **Copying onto a drive in Finder** failed with "you don't have permission
  to access some of the items". Finder's extra file information (tags,
  quarantine, provenance) is now accepted and set aside rather than refused,
  so copies go through and nothing extra is stored in the drive.
- If a drive can't be mounted, the unlock dialog now shows the mount
  driver's full message, and you can select and copy it.
- The Mac app's Dock icon is the same size as its neighbours, and the window
  buttons are top left where Mac windows have them.

## Faster on macOS

- Finder no longer re-asks for every file's details every second, and
  folder listings and lookups run side by side instead of queueing behind
  each other. The biggest difference is in folders with many files.
- A file's modified date in Finder can lag by up to a minute after it's
  changed; its contents are always current.

## Known limitations

- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
